standards.standardUsageTips: CEDS is the hub. A CEDS HubReference is a tuple: domain class + property + range [+ value], keyed by canonicalKey (the CEDS Global ID). It decomposes via HAS_CEDS_DOMAIN / HAS_CEDS_PROPERTY / HAS_CEDS_RANGE / HAS_CEDS_VALUE / HAS_CEDS_QUALIFIER; its range may be an option set, another CEDS class (a reference), or a datatype. Present a CEDS anchor as its full tuple — domain · property · range [· value], the cedsTuple field from dme_find_mappings — never as a bare Global ID: the Global ID is the tuple's durable key, not its meaning.

standards.standardUsageTips: PESC keeps its mappings on INSTANCE nodes. A PESC element declaration (DmeProperty, the node search finds) carries no match edge; it has one occurrence (DmeInstance) per place it appears in the document, reached by HAS_INSTANCE, and the occurrences carry the mappings. They arrive as dme_find_mappings rows with direction 'outgoingViaInstance' (or rows carrying instanceGroupList / instanceCount / viaInstanceGroupList), and in dme_graph_retriever as instanceView.mappingsViaInstances. Group them by the occurrence's sectionPath, e.g. CollegeTranscript/Student/Person: present each hub concept ONCE with the document sections that hold it and the instance count, never one repeated line per instance. If different sections carry different hub concepts for the same element, say so plainly — the meaning differs by context; it is not an error. Each PESC release (College Transcript, High School Transcript, …) is its own standard with its own card.

standards.standardUsageTips: PESC_LD is a SHACL application profile, not a vocabulary: a DmeClass is a SHAPE (a node shape that targets a class) and a DmeProperty is one ROW of the profile (one property as constrained on one shape). Most rows borrow their term from another standard; the borrowed term is on the node as termCurie (as the source writes it, e.g. ceterms:name) and termIri (expanded from the package's own namespaces.csv). The same borrowed term can appear on several shapes, so search by termCurie returns one row per shape. Picklists are DmeOptionSet nodes owned by their row.
standards.descriptionSource: a TAP row's 'note' column, its usage note, carried verbatim as description (and as usageNote): it is not a definition; the package publishes labels and usage notes only, no definitions, so a row without a note and every shape carry no description

standards.standardUsageTips: SIF keeps its mappings on INSTANCE nodes. A SIF Question (DmeProperty, the node search finds) carries no match edge; it has one Field (DmeInstance) per object it appears in, reached by HAS_INSTANCE, and the Fields carry the mappings. They arrive as dme_find_mappings rows with direction 'outgoingViaInstance' (or rows carrying instanceGroupList / instanceCount / viaInstanceGroupList), and in dme_graph_retriever as instanceView.mappingsViaInstances. Group them by the owning object, (object)-[:HAS_FIELD]->(field), e.g. StudentPersonal, StaffPersonal: present each hub concept ONCE with the objects that hold it and the instance count, never one repeated line per instance. If different objects carry different hub concepts for the same Question, say so plainly — the meaning differs by context; it is not an error. Structure: HAS_FIELD reads 'object has field', HAS_CHILD 'element contains element' (Object -> Container -> Container|Field).
